question: A joinery audit ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two batches of 46 and 12 identical panels are stacked into equal full piles, using the largest pile size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage of mass 167 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pile size. The saw drive must supply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and the audit records that force in kilonewtons. To the record 25 is added, in those same kilonewton units, as the clamp preload. Eleven carriages run per shop, and the firm has 5 shops. What number ends the audit, in kN?
Solving x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0 for the larger root is 8 m/s^2. A 127 kg mass produces force = 1016 N, converted to kN, scaled by 9, decreased by 14. A threshold is 100 kN. What is the final force in kN?

A velodrome audit ends with one figure in kilojoules. The test sled's mass plate reads 12000 g. The sled's speed, in metres per second, is how fast the slope of the curve y = 3x^3 - 4x^2 is itself changing at x = 3. The energy the moving sled carries is the base value, which the audit records in kilojoules. Eight sleds run per session, and the venue holds 7 identical sessions. The track surface is 42 mm thick, which is irrelevant here. What figure ends the audit, in kJ?

A crane works needs the total figure, in kilonewtons, for a hoist installation. The drum's position along its guide is, in metres, 2*t^3 + 3*t^2 with t in seconds, and the rating is taken at the instant t = 4 s by differentiating that position 2 times to give the carriage's rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 178 kg, and the machine house is at 18 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the result is expressed in kilonewtons. A tower carries 8 identical hoists, and the works has 11 identical towers. What total figure, in kN, does the installation show?

Integrating 4x² + 6x from 0 to 1 gives 4/3 m/s, scaled by 3 gives 4 m/s² acceleration. A 78 kg object produces force. Multiplied by 10, multiplied by 8, and converted to kilonewtons. What is the final force in kN?

A depot ships 250 crates of one kind and 234 of another, and the loader stacks them into identical columns using the largest column height that divides both totals exactly. A test cart is then sent down the ramp at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that column height plus 27. The cart has a mass of 41000 g, and the ramp is lit by a 60 W lamp. The energy audit takes the cart's kinetic energy in kilojoules, subtracts 23 kJ booked to the hoist and then a further 6 kJ booked to the door motor. What does the energy audit report, in kJ?
The second derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 at x=2 is 12. A 39 kg object develops kinetic energy. After converting to kJ, scaling by 2, and subtracting 9, what is the final energy in kilojoules?

A 42 kg mail cart rolls off a loading ramp. The ramp is 3 m long. The cart's speed, in m/s, is 2 times the larger root of x² - 5x + 6 = 0. On the way across the dock, the cart loses 20 J of its energy of motion to a rough joint and another 17 J to a door threshold, then gains 10 J from a downward slope. What is the cart's energy of motion, in J, after the slope?

The definite integral of 1*x^2 + 6*x from 1 to 3 equals 32. A 47-kilogram object at 32 m/s has kinetic energy calculated from half mass times velocity squared. Add 6, add 19, convert from joules to kilojoules, and subtract 30. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A fleet controller wants the total force, in newtons, needed when 11 regions, each with 12 depots, each with 8 sites, each with 12 identical carts, all accelerate their carts at once. Each cart has a mass of 79 kg. The acceleration, in m/s², is the larger root of x² - 6x + 8 = 0. What total force, in N, is needed?

A gravel plant's shift total is 9 times a single skip's net figure, expressed in kilojoules. A skip's net figure is its kinetic energy less 15 J absorbed by the buffer and a further 3 J lost in the latch. The skip has a mass of 39 kg. Its distance along the incline, in metres, is 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 4 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the plant uses how fast it is moving at the instant 2 seconds after release. What is the plant's shift total, in kJ?

The figure a crane operator records, in kN, is 8 times a single-cable net force that is expressed in kN. The single-cable net force is 7 N less than the force needed to accelerate a 176,000 g load at a rate in m/s² equal to the slope of the curve y = 3x³ - 4x² at the point x = 1. Eight identical cables share the load. What figure does the operator record, in kN?
Quadratic x² - 10x + 21 = 0 smaller root 3. A 2 kg object energy increased 22 J, converted kJ, scaled 11.
Integration: 3x^2 + x from 0 to 1 equals 5/2. A 20-kilogram system at 5/2 m/s² generates force. Subtract 9, subtract 28, scale by 11. Lot: 2024-001, not used. What is the force in N?

A yard holds 129 clamps and 375 pins, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to a trolley whose mass is 42000 g. The force the drive must apply to the trolley to accelerate it at that rate is calculated. Because 5 identical trolleys run from one drawbar the drawbar force is 5 times that, and a slack allowance of 3 N is then subtracted. The whole drawbar assembly is repeated on 4 tracks and the loads add. What is the total load, in N?

A design expression evaluates 6 × (7 + 3) in m/s, giving an acceleration through arithmetic. A 157 kg mass experiences this acceleration. The resulting force is multiplied by 4 through the mechanical system. Subtracting 28 N for friction losses gives the net force. Convert this to kilonewtons for the structural rating. What is the final rated force in kN? (The operating frequency is 60 Hz, which is not used.)

Two shaft encoders on a test rig cycle through 242 and 21 ticks per run. The largest whole number that divides evenly into both counts is the speed, in meters per second, of a 52 kg flywheel. Find its kinetic energy, convert it to kilojoules, multiply by 5 for a five-flywheel bank, subtract 24 kilojoules for a shared baseline, and multiply the total by 3 for a three-bank facility. A separate voltmeter nearby reads 21 volts, unrelated to this calculation. What is the final energy, in kilojoules, for the facility?

On a lab test bench, two speeds, in m/s, sum to 11 and multiply to 24; the smaller is kept, multiplied by 8, and then 19 m/s is added. This total speed belongs to a slider whose mass is stated as 38 kg. A separate voltmeter reads 4 V, unrelated to this task. The slider's kinetic energy is converted into kilojoules, and finally scaled by a factor of 10. What is the final energy, in kilojoules?

What the rail-yard engineer ultimately wants is the total energy in kilojoules for 12 identical wagons, each corrected for coupling losses. Each wagon has a mass of 54000 g and moves at a speed in metres per second found by taking 9 times the sum of 8 and 1 and subtracting 29. Find the kinetic energy of one wagon in joules, subtract 4 J for the energy lost in its coupling, and convert the result to kilojoules. Multiply by 12 for all the wagons. What is the total in kJ?

A tunnel-boring contractor closes its thrust sheet with one figure in kN. The shield segment being pushed has a mass of 100 kg. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is the area under the curve 1*x**2 + 0*x between x = 1 and x = 3. The segment ring is 6 m across, a dimension on the drawing that is not used in the thrust number. To the force on the segment the contractor adds 26 N for the seal drag, then writes the total in kN and subtracts 27 for the grout pressure credit. The sheet multiplies that by 6 because 6 jacks act together. What figure in kN closes the thrust sheet?

Arithmetic: 4 × (6 + 2) = 32, then 32 - 7 = 25. Scaled by 3 gives 75 m/s. With 35 kg, energy = 0.5 × 35 × 5625 = 98437.5 J, converted to kilojoules, increased by 27. The device's serial is XYZ789, not relevant. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

The greatest common divisor of 339 and 86 is 1. Multiply by 3 to get 3. A 20-kilogram object at 3 m/s has kinetic energy calculated from half mass times velocity squared. Subtract 5 and convert from joules to kilojoules. What is the final energy in kilojoules? A distance of 50 meters was noted.

The second derivative of 4x^3 - 3x^2 at x = 2 is 36 m/s^2. A 55 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 6, increased by 16, decreased by 26, converted to kJ. A reference is 100 m/s^2. What is the final energy in kJ?

A test bench drives a slide of 110000 grams, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 4t^2 + 8t. Between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second the acceleration accumulates from zero, and the value reached at t = 1 second is the acceleration used. From the force needed to drive the slide the controller subtracts a bearing tare of 9 N and then adds a mounting allowance of 5 N. The result is multiplied by 7, because 7 slides run on the bench. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?

A system determines a critical parameter by solving x^2 - 7*x + 10 = 0 and selecting the smaller root. A 99 kg apparatus experiences an acceleration equal to this parameter (in m/s^2). The resulting force is measured, converted to kilonewtons, scaled by a factor of 8, and then 12 kilonewtons are subtracted. Finally, the result is multiplied by 7. The nearby pressure gauge reads 200 kPa but is not used in this problem. What is the final value in newtons?
